item.text: {"branches":[{"elimination_condition":"Eliminate if the estimated catch-rate difference between livebait groups and no-livebait groups is below 0 fish per hour after accounting for hours, persons, children, and camper status.","hypothesis_id":"H1","intervention":"Stratify or model trips by livebait status while holding hours, persons, child count, and camper status constant; calibrate catch and hours using recorded units and inspect duplicated or impossible records.","mechanism":"Live bait increases fishing effectiveness, producing a higher fish-caught rate per hour.","mechanism_key":"livebait_positive_effect","predictions":[{"direction":"higher","discriminator_id":"D1","failure_condition":"The livebait-associated catch-rate increase is absent, reverses, or is not robust after adjustment and calibration.","observable":"Adjusted mean fish caught per hour for trips using livebait versus trips not using livebait.","prediction_id":"P1","value_range":null}]},{"elimination_condition":"Eliminate if the estimated livebait catch-rate difference remains materially positive after adjustment for trip duration, group composition, camper status, and measurement checks.","hypothesis_id":"H2","intervention":"Compare calibrated fish-caught rates by livebait status with frozen covariate controls for hours, persons, child count, and camper status; verify the negative control shows no spurious bait association.","mechanism":"Live bait does not causally affect catch rate; apparent differences arise from group composition, trip selection, or other confounding.","mechanism_key":"livebait_null_confounding","predictions":[{"direction":"similar","discriminator_id":"D1","failure_condition":"A consistent, substantively large livebait-associated increase remains after covariate adjustment and negative-control calibration.","observable":"Adjusted mean fish caught per hour for trips using livebait versus trips not using livebait.","prediction_id":"P2","value_range":null}]},{"elimination_condition":"Eliminate if the livebait association is stable and positive across calibrated subsets and is not explained by recording artifacts, exposure differences, or covariate adjustment.","hypothesis_id":"H3","intervention":"Estimate catch rates using a measurement-error-sensitive model, test results across hours and group-size strata, and perform calibration checks on units, zero values, and duplicated observations.","mechanism":"The observed livebait difference is primarily a measurement or exposure artifact, such as misrecorded hours, bait status, or non-comparable fishing exposure.","mechanism_key":"measurement_exposure_artifact","predictions":[{"direction":"unstable_or_reversed","discriminator_id":"D1","failure_condition":"The livebait catch-rate difference remains consistently positive and similar across calibration checks and prespecified strata.","observable":"Adjusted mean fish caught per hour for trips using livebait versus trips not using livebait across measurement-calibrated subsets.","prediction_id":"P3","value_range":null}]}],"budget_units":3,"question":"How does livebait status discriminate among a positive-effect, null-confounding, and measurement/exposure-artifact explanation of visitors' fish caught per hour, after calibration and adjustment for hours, group composition, and camper status?"}
